source_intake.temporal_skew_assessment: No catastrophic calendar interval hole was found; every month contains more than 2,500 unique arXiv papers. Six capped cs.LG month slices and present-day publisher-index archival limits remain the material completeness risks.

annual_phase_candidates.interpretation: Scaling Laws, Meena, REALM, Turing-NLG and DeepSpeed/ZeRO make scale, dialogue, external knowledge and large-model systems visible as separate design problems before GPT-3 dominates the year's public narrative.

DPR and BlenderBot are followed by Jukebox, RAG, GPT-3, the OpenAI API, Image GPT, DDPM and GShard, concentrating scale, access, retrieval, dialogue, media generation and systems design into the year's densest architectural transition.

The emphasis shifts from model demonstrations toward access, steering and evaluation boundaries: human-feedback summarization, toxicity evaluation, the RAG release boundary and Microsoft GPT-3 licensing clarify how models are used, controlled and assessed.

CrowS-Pairs, DDIM, score-SDE and Taming Transformers refine the evaluation and generative-media branches; the year closes with multiple viable generation paradigms rather than one settled architecture, forming the handoff into 2021.

annual_trajectories: scale and in-context capability: empirical scaling laws and GPT-3 connect frontier scale to few-shot/in-context task behavior
access and distribution: API service boundaries and licensing separate model capability from who can use or integrate it
retrieval and external knowledge: REALM, DPR and RAG move knowledge access from parameters alone toward explicit retrieval
dialogue systems: Meena and BlenderBot expose scale, evaluation and system-recipe questions specific to open-domain conversation
systems scaling: DeepSpeed/ZeRO and GShard make memory partitioning, sharding and conditional computation first-class scale constraints
generative-media branching: autoregressive image/audio/discrete-token approaches coexist with diffusion and score-based generation
steering, evaluation and risk: human preference feedback and toxicity/bias benchmarks establish early post-training and model-behavior evaluation layers
editorial_thesis: 2020年、生成AIは単なる『巨大モデル競争』から、scaleを設計原理として明示し、その能力をfew-shot/in-context behavior、API access、retrieval、human feedback、dialogue、distributed systems、image/audio/diffusion generationへ枝分かれさせ始めた。Scaling LawsとGPT-3はscaleからcapabilityへ向かう軸を、OpenAI APIはaccess/distribution境界を、REALMとRAGはmodel-external knowledgeを、MeenaとBlenderBotはdialogue system designを、DeepSpeed/ZeROとGShardはscaleを成立させるsystems layerを、DDPM・score-SDEとImage GPT・Taming Transformersは複数のgenerative-media系譜を、human-feedback summarizationとtoxicity/bias評価はsteering/evaluation/risk layerの萌芽を示した。2020年は、2021年の『同じ基盤を再利用・適応・接続する多層システム』への前段として読む。

comparison_dimensions: scaling relation versus observed few-shot capability
model release versus API access versus technology license
retrieval pretraining versus dense retrieval infrastructure versus retrieval-conditioned generation
dialogue scaling/evaluation versus dialogue system recipe/release
parameter count versus memory/sharding/conditional-compute systems design
autoregressive/discrete media generation versus diffusion/score-based generation
human-feedback steering versus benchmark-based behavior/risk evaluation
reclassification_decisions: OpenAI API is treated as an access/interface boundary, not as a separate model family.
DeepSpeed/ZeRO is treated as systems infrastructure, not as a model capability event.
REALM and RealToxicityPrompts are selected as SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE because they strengthen retrieval and risk trajectories without needing independent primary package placement.
DDIM, StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs, Turing-NLG, Jukebox, DPR, the Microsoft GPT-3 license and the duplicate Scaling Laws publication boundary remain Evidence HOLD items.
The Pile remains a preserved year-boundary raw observation and is not promoted into the 2020 Evidence core.
Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback is framed as preference-feedback steering and not retroactively equated with the later full RLHF stack.

chronology_plan.rule: Distinct paper, release, access and licensing boundaries remain separate chronology rows even when they belong to one Evidence series.

notable_hold_outs: Scaling Laws first-party publication duplicate boundary
screening_dropped_but_raw_preserved_exam: the remainder of the 45,116 normalized discovery records not required to establish the selected annual trajectories
residual_claim_boundaries: Vendor, project and author performance/capability/safety evaluations remain attributed rather than treated as independently reproduced results.
Paper first-publication, first-party announcement/release, API availability and technology licensing remain distinct chronology states.
Six capped cs.LG query slices mean the broad arXiv intake cannot establish historical absence; exact-identity checks protect material selected anchors rather than proving a census.
Current publisher indexes cannot prove that every 2020 first-party page remains linked or byte-identical to its original publication state.
The configured GitHub Release watchlist yielded no normalized 2020 release records; commit-level ecosystem history is not reconstructed exhaustively.
Bias/toxicity benchmark coverage is representative of an emerging evaluation layer and is not an exhaustive safety taxonomy.
The 2020 human-feedback evidence is a steering precursor and must not be described as if the later end-to-end RLHF product stack were already established.

single_volume_coherence.assessment: The seven annual trajectories interact strongly enough to support a single 2020 volume and create a coherent handoff into SP-2021-Y. No Evidence-backed need to split 2020 into H1/H2 was found.
